record.original_question: For every bridgeless cubic graph G, does there exist a homomorphism from its line graph L(G) to the line graph of the Petersen graph L(P)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4 Let G be a bridgeless cubic graph and let P be the Petersen graph. Then there is a homomorphism from the line graph L(G) to L(P ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P denote the Petersen graph, i.e. the unique 3-regular graph on 10 vertices whose vertex set is the collection of 2-element subsets of {1,2,3,4,5} with two vertices adjacent iff the subsets are disjoint. For any graph H, let L(H) be its line graph, whose vertices are the edges of H and in which two vertices are adjacent iff the corresponding edges of H share an endpoint. A graph homomorphism from a graph X to a graph Y is a map f: V(X) → V(Y) such that whenever uv ∈ E(X), one has f(u)f(v) ∈ E(Y). A graph is called bridgeless if it has no edge whose removal disconnects a connected component, and cubic if every vertex has degree 3.

Prove or disprove: for every bridgeless cubic graph G, there exists a graph homomorphism from L(G) to L(P).
artifact.status_search_result: The Petersen colouring conjecture, formulated by Jaeger in 1985, remains open. Recent works (e.g., Mkrtchyan 2012; Hägglund–Steffen and Mazzuoccolo–Tabarelli "Variations on the Petersen colouring conjecture", 2020) continue to study and propose weakenings of the conjecture, and the Open Problem Garden lists it as unresolved. It is known to imply both the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture and the cycle double cover conjecture.

status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture (Jaeger): Every bridgeless cubic graph admits a Petersen colouring.

status_evidence.title: Variations on the Petersen colouring conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Few progress has been made on the Petersen coloring conjecture; possible counter-examples remain elusive.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture still open as of recent work.

status_evidence.title: A remark on Petersen coloring conjecture of Jaeger
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates implications of the conjecture without resolving it.
